A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM FROM MEETING OF
  FEBRUARY 15, 2022: TENNIS COURT RESURFACING AND PICKLEBALL
  OVERLAYS

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve a contract with Trueline Construction
  & Surfacing Inc. in the amount of $55,722.40 for the resurfacing of the Rolling Hills
  Estates Tennis Club tennis courts with the addition of four pickleball court overlays.

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief staff report (as per the agenda
material).

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA expressed concern about the small number of residents
surveyed regarding interest in adding the pickleball courts. Community Services Supervisor
Pinuelas explained that pickleball is a fast growing sport and in talking with other neighboring
cities who currently offer pickleball, typically once people know it is available the program grows
quickly.

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas explained that the bulk of the proposed cost is for
the court resurfacing, and that the cost to add the pickleball court overlays is $325 each for two
courts, which is significantly lower than if they were to be added outside of the resurfacing

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
FEBRUARY 22, 2022
 project. She added that the court resurfacing typically occurs every four to eight years, in
response to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF also clarified that the cost proposed is for the total tennis court
resurfacing project, and noted that courts with pickleball overlays can still be used as tennis
courts.

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas noted that staff has contacted RHE Resident Tennis
Pro, Bob Krueger, who agreed that the two proposed courts would be the best courts to put
the pickleball overlays on.

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas explained there will be two pickleball overlays per
tennis court, one on each half of the court with the portable pickleball nets moved into place
when in use, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN.

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the project is expected to be completed
in two to four weeks, beginning in March, in response to MAYOR ZERUNYAN.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No additional public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE A CONTRACT WITH TRUELINE CONSTRUCTION &
  SURFACING INC. IN THE AMOUNT OF $55,722.40 FOR THE
  RESURFACING OF THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES TENNIS CLUB TENNIS
  COURTS WITH THE ADDITION OF FOUR PICKLEBALL COURT
  OVERLAYS.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

**ITEM TAKEN OUT OF ORDER**

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2501 OPPOSING INITIATIVE 21-0042A1, "THE

C.  RESOLUTION NO. 2500 AUTHORIZING SUBMITTAL OF APPLICATION FOR
  CALIFORNIA CLIMATE INVESTMENT FIRE PREVENTION GRANT PROGRAM

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt the attached Resolution No. 2500,
  authorizing staff to receive granted funds from CAL FIRE’s Fire Prevention Grant
  program and designating the City Manager, or his designee, as a “Signature Authority.”

Management Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Management Analyst Slawson noted that the grant is project-specific, and that the City would
apply for a $15,000 grant for the project as recommended by the CAL FIRE Unit designated
to Los Angeles County along with the Fire Captain at Los Angeles County Fire Station 106,
in response to MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA, AS
  FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2500, AUTHORIZING STAFF TO RECEIVE
  GRANTED FUNDS FROM CAL FIRE’S FIRE PREVENTION GRANT
  PROGRAM AND DESIGNATING THE CITY MANAGER, OR HIS DESIGNEE,
  AS A “SIGNATURE AUTHORITY.”

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

D.  REVIEW OF PROPOSED MUNICIPAL CODE AMENDMENTS TO IMPLEMENT THE
  REQUIREMENTS OF SENATE BILL 9

  Recommendation: That the City Council review the proposed Municipal Code
  amendments to implement SB-9, including the adoption of objective development
  standards and procedures permitted under SB-9, and provide direction so that a final
  ordinance may be presented for adoption.

City Attorney Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA thanked City Attorney Davis for a clear and understandable
report. Discussion ensued about Home Owner’s Associations’ (HOA) role in enforcement and
the requirement of recorded declaration of an HOA in order to be recognized.

City Attorney Davis noted that setbacks vary depending on the side of the structure. Planning
Manager Naughton further explained that typical side-yard setbacks for one story structures
are 10 feet from a side property line, and get larger with two story structures. She also noted
that new laws allow cities to have objective design guidelines but that cities can’t preclude units
that are at least 800 square feet in size and can be as close as four feet to a side property line,
which is very similar to the new Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) laws, in response to COUNCIL
MEMBER ZUCKERMAN.

Discussion ensued regarding the proposed Exceptions to Development Standards in
Section H, in response to MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
FEBRUARY 22, 2022
 COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA highlighted the fact that newly constructed buildings must
meet new fire hardening requirements yet retrofitting is not required of existing structures.
She further expressed her concern and frustration with housing density requirements from
the State when the City is in a high-fire hazard area.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN echoed COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA’s frustration with the State’s
requirements of SB-9.

City Attorney Davis highlighted Section E, Subsection 2(b) of 16.06.050, noting the building
official will have the authority to make findings based on a preponderance of evidence of a
potential health and safety issue, in response to MAYOR ZERUNYAN’s concerns regarding
increasing the City’s density with the egress challenges the City would already face in the event
of a wildfire or major catastrophe.

City Attorney Davis stated that staff does not expect to have a large number of applications,
and emphasized that each project will be carefully reviewed.

Discussion continued about fire safety and evacuation concerns, and how it relates to the SB-
9 requirements.

City Attorney Davis requested direction from Council regarding the proposed exceptions in
Section 17.80.040 Subsection H, and the order of said exceptions.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA suggested moving horse keeping area higher on the list of
priorities, since the City is an equestrian community.

City Attorney Davis highlighted the Notice of Application section of Section 17.80.050.

City Attorney Davis confirmed that the Director providing ministerial approvals would be David
Wahba, Director of Community Development & Public Works or his designee, in response to
COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

Planning Manager Naughton noted that staff’s first priority would be to reduce the 35 foot
spacing requirement before reducing the size of a horse keeping area.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN suggested a “Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)” document be created
in an effort to educate the community, describing the SB-9 requirements and what we’ve done
in the City within the bounds of the law to accommodate SB-9 within our community.

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba highlighted that the City is within the
high-fire hazard severity zone, noting there are additional requirements from the Los Angeles
County Fire Department and Los Angeles County Building & Safety Department.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ, AS
  FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE PROPOSED MUNICIPAL CODE AMENDMENT TEXT TO
  IMPLEMENT SB-9, INCLUDING THE ADOPTION OF OBJECTIVE
  DEVELOPMENT STANDARDS AND PROCEDURES PERMITTED UNDER
  SB-9, FOR INCLUSION IN A FINAL ORDINANCE TO BE PRESENTED AT

B.  UPDATE ON LOS ANGELES COUNTY SAFER AT HOME ORDER AND STATUS OF
  CITY EVENTS (VERBAL REPORT)

City Manager Grammer reported that the daily COVID-19 case rates and hospitalization rates
have been steadily declining over the last few weeks, and the State has lifted the state-wide
indoor mask requirement. The indoor mask mandate still remains in place for Los Angeles
County at this time.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF reported that the Peninsula Holiday Parade Subcommittee met to
debrief from the event in December.

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF reported that the South Bay Cities Council of Government’s
(SBCCOG) General Assembly will be held Thursday, March, 24, 2022 in Carson.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN reported on the Regional Contract Law Committee and Peninsula Public
Safety Committee meetings that took place in February. He announced that COUNCIL
MEMBER ZUCKERMAN has been elected Chair of both the Peninsula Public Safety and
Regional Contract Law Committees. He also reported that the Palos Verdes Peninsula School
District has been awarded a grant through the California Department of Justice to assist with
the cost of school resource officers (SRO). The grant will also offset the City’s cost share for
the SROs. Lastly, he reported that the Peninsula cities are working together to explore wildfire
and disaster mitigation efforts such as wildfire cameras and evacuation planning.
